mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a GLC 300d engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A GLC 300d engine replacement typically costs between £2,800 and £4,800 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. OM654 2.0-litre diesel units range from £2,800 to £4,800 supply only. Rebuilt OM654 (GLC 300d): £2,800-£4,800 supply only. Reconditioned units: £2,400-£3,800. Used engines from breakers: £1,800-£3,200 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the OM654 engine in the GLC 300d reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654 is a highly refined and efficient engine - a significant improvement over the OM651 it replaced. However, it has several well-documented issues. EGR cooler cracking - the dominant failure driver. NOx sensor failure and AdBlue system crystallisation. Rocker arm bearing and camshaft lobe wear. Timing chain wear on higher-mileage units. With regular maintenance, 150,000+ miles is realistic.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM654 EGR cooler failure in a GLC 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654's EGR cooler typically fails between 40,000-80,000 miles, with several warning signs. Coolant level dropping with no visible external leak. White smoke from the exhaust. Check engine light illuminated. Decrease in engine performance and rough idle. Increased fuel consumption.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my GLC 300d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., EGR cooler, NOx sensors, AdBlue injector). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic valve train failure. EGR cooler replacement at specialist: £700-£1,100 - excellent value if caught early. NOx sensor pair replacement: £350-£600 - replace both as a pair. Full OM654 rebuild: £3,800-£5,800 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given GLC 300d values (£18,000-£50,000+), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my GLC 300d has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. GLC 300d (X253, 2019-2022): OM654.920 (2.0L diesel, 245hp). GLC 300d (X254, 2022-present): OM654.820 (2.0L diesel, 269hp). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used GLC 300d engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a GLC 300d. The longitudinal engine layout, 9G-Tronic gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Longitudinal engine mounting requires specialist alignment. 9G-Tronic transmission alignment needs precise setup. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class 300d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz GLC 300d relies on the OM654 2.0-litre modular diesel - a lightweight, all-aluminium engine praised for refinement and efficiency, but not without its vulnerabilities. EGR cooler cracking, NOx sensor failure, rocker arm bearing wear, and timing chain issues dominate replacement demand. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common GLC 300d engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM654 EGR Cooler Cracking - Why the GLC 300d Loses Coolant
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC 300d (OM654.920, OM654.820, 2019-present)
problems.rootCause: The original EGR cooler (part A6540940101) suffers thermal stress fractures, allowing coolant to enter the exhaust system, triggering low coolant warnings, misfires, and eventually engine overheating. Coolant loss without a visible external leak is often the first sign of EGR cooler failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed EGR cooler with revised OEM unit, drain and refill coolant, clear fault codes
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-80k miles. Viable if caught early with no overheating damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: EGR cooler replacement plus intake manifold cleaning to remove coolant residue and carbon
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-80k miles. Required if coolant has fouled intake valves

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM654 with upgraded EGR cooler, new gaskets, timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when coolant ingestion has damaged cylinders

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical GLC 300d (X253, 2019-2022) is worth £18,000-£35,000, while a second-generation X254 (2022-present) retains values of £35,000-£50,000+ - the full replacement cost of £3,800-£5,800 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples, making a specialist rebuilt engine a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: If caught early with no overheating damage, replace just the EGR cooler - specialist pricing beats dealer by 30-40%. However, many cases present after coolant loss has caused cylinder head damage. On a GLC 300d worth £18,000-£35,000, the full engine replacement with upgraded cooler is often the safer long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM654 prices for your Mercedes GLC 300d

problems.group: OM654 NOx Sensor & AdBlue System Failure
problems.h4: OM654 NOx Sensor & AdBlue System Failure - Why the GLC 300d Triggers Emissions Warnings
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC 300d (OM654.920, OM654.820, 2019-present)
problems.rootCause: NOx sensors fail due to internal heating element degradation, causing permanent emissions warning lights. AdBlue crystallises inside the injector nozzle, blocking flow and triggering countdown start inhibitors. These emissions system failures are a dominant driver of GLC 300d workshop visits.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injector, ultrasonic clean nozzle, perform SCR system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-60k miles. Preventative, not a permanent fix

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace upstream and downstream NOx sensors, clear fault codes, road test
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-80k miles. Replace both sensors as a pair to avoid repeat visits

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue injector, flush tank and lines, reset SCR counter with diagnostic tool
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-80k miles. Required if crystallisation has damaged the module

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM654 with new emissions components, EGR cooler, DPF professionally cleaned
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for persistent emissions failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLC 300d worth £18,000-£50,000+, replacing NOx sensors and AdBlue components individually is sensible. However, if you're facing a third emissions component failure within 12 months, price up a full rebuilt engine - the labour to repeatedly access the SCR system becomes uneconomical.
problems.recommendation: For a GLC 300d still under 60,000 miles, replace the AdBlue injector and NOx sensors individually as they fail - but always replace both NOx sensors as a pair (upstream and downstream) to avoid repeat workshop visits. If emissions warnings persist after component replacement, have the entire SCR system inspected before committing to further repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare OM654 emissions repair quotes for your GLC 300d

problems.group: OM654 Rocker Arm Bearing & Timing Chain Wear
problems.h4: OM654 Rocker Arm Bearing & Timing Chain Wear - Long-Term GLC 300d Reliability Concerns
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLC Class GLC 300d (OM654.920, OM654.820, 2019-present)
problems.rootCause: The OM654 has a documented issue with failing rocker arm bearings and damaged camshaft lobes. Timing chain wear causing rattle on cold start has also been reported. These issues typically manifest on higher-mileage examples and can lead to catastrophic engine failure if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect rocker arms and camshaft lobes, replace individual failed components
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles. Viable if caught early with no camshaft damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshafts, rocker arms, bearings, timing chain components
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles. Required if rocker bearing failure has damaged camshafts

repairOptions.tier: Major - Full Timing Chain & Valve Train Set
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, camshafts, rocker arms, bearings
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles. Corrects all valve train weaknesses

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM654 with new valve train, timing components, upgraded parts
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLC 300d worth £18,000-£50,000+, timing chain and rocker arm replacement at £2,000-£3,200 is a justifiable investment. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The OM654's rocker arm bearing failure can appear with minimal warning. If you hear unusual tapping or ticking from the engine, have the valve train inspected immediately. On higher-mileage GLC 300d examples (80,000+ miles), a full rebuilt engine with upgraded valve train components eliminates all common failure points in one go - often more cost-effective than piecemeal repairs.
